assumptions_challenged: MISEV2023 guidance is sufficient to define program-specific validation criteria and substitute for validated assay and manufacturing data for SGL-001
Key analytical assays (intact‑EV identity, LLOQ, specificity, precision) are already in place or can be validated in a short (3‑month) timeline
Three GMP‑like reproducible batches with release/stability/potency data can be produced and documented within the proposed schedule
A GLP‑like large‑animal intranasal biodistribution/tox study with intact‑EV attribution controls can be designed, executed, and reported within the same 3‑month period
Formulation/device intact‑EV recovery and compatibility studies sufficient to support in vivo bridging can be completed rapidly and will be straightforward to interpret
falsification_conditions: Provide program‑specific MCB/WCB establishment records (characterization, generation dates, SOPs) that predate the decision point

Supply fit‑for‑purpose assay validation reports for each orthogonal QC assay and intact‑EV identity/potency assays including documented LLOQ, specificity, accuracy, precision, linearity, and robustness
Submit a stability‑indicating potency assay development report demonstrating correlation to a defined in vivo PD endpoint (data and statistical correlation analysis)

Deliver full reports for ≥3 GMP‑like manufacturing runs with release testing, impurity/particle/protein/lipid profiles, comparability analyses, and stability data demonstrating lot‑to‑lot reproducibility

Provide formulation/device compatibility and intact‑EV recovery studies (ex vivo and in vivo where applicable) with controls showing preservation of intact EV attributes after processing and administration

Produce a GLP‑like large‑animal intranasal biodistribution/toxicity study report including intact‑EV attribution controls (eg. orthogonal detection methods, negative controls for non‑vesicular signal), study plan/preregistration, raw data, and statistical analysis
strongest_objection: The proposed Stage-1 gating package and 3-month timeline rest on conflating high-level consensus guidance (MISEV2023) with program-level validated data and operational capacity; the evidence provided is guidance only and does not demonstrate that SGL-001 already meets the specific, technical CMC/analytics/GLP requirements or that these activities (assay development/validation, three GMP-like runs, stability/potency correlation, and a GLP-like large-animal intranasal study with intact‑EV attribution controls) can be completed to a regulatory‑acceptable standard within the proposed 3-month window.
